headline.line: A crowdsourced framework for mapping urban-scale window views from real estate imagery

synthesis.deviation_note: 1 day(s) of archive inside the 30-day window; 7 needed before a deviation means anything
synthesis.paragraph: Three papers today carry the tag "Urban Planning and Governance," focusing on reimagining urban planning for disaster resilience in South Africa, exploring the associations between digitalization and space-time flexibilities in Beijing, and examining adult-centrism and youth exclusion in urban environments. Outside of this group, one study developed a crowdsourced framework to map urban-scale window view perceptions using real estate imagery from Wuhan, China. Another paper established a conceptual framework linking out-of-home toilet access, transport disadvantage, and dignified ageing in Africa. Finally, a third independent study applied deep learning-based natural language processing models to classify wrong-way driving crashes from police-written narratives.
